email.body:
Tanya, you said today, in the delivery routing ruling: "we route every reaction through one bundle per run per person, not one message per skill — a person should get one thing to read, not four." You also said "the bundle closes when the run closes, and a skill that misses the close waits for the next run rather than sending on its own." The memory records that Tina pushed back on the batching window, and that you held the close rule against her objection. The per-skill alternative, with client-side collapsing, was considered and rejected, because it moves the ordering problem onto the reader.

Reactions from a run now go out as one bundle per person per run, and the bundle closes with the run. A skill that finishes after the close waits for the next run instead of sending on its own. Per-skill delivery is no longer the design.

That suggests to me that the reaction-delivery doc in the repo, which describes each skill sending its own message as soon as it finishes, is out of date. If that holds, a skill that finishes late will reach people a run later than it does today, and people should expect that gap. I read the close rule as the answer to the batching objection, but Tina's own words are not in the memory, so that is only my read.

Two questions. Does Tina's objection to the batching window still stand, or does the close rule answer it fully? Should the reaction-delivery doc be rewritten to describe the bundle, or kept as the description of the old way?
